main_text.p: runt, non pauci gramen & herbā in ore habere conspiciebantur. Milites nostri his visis, commiseratione moti, relictis castris domum redierunt, neue cogerentur tantas miserias aspicere militiam eiurabant.

Anno 1570. & sequentibus aliquot annis in Austria etiam & per Germaniā, multi fame consumpti sunt. Item in Italia, multi interiere, alii ne eundē vitæ finē haberent, & fame tabescerent, nauarchis ad remigia operā suam obtulerunt, voluntariē id supplicij genus subierunt, quod non nisi furibus & nebulonibus infligi solet. O malesuada fames.

An. 1572. Sæuiebat in Occitana et in maritima quidem ora, soli alioqui feracissimi regione, grauissima fames: ut passim enectorum cadauera in viis obversarentur lib.10. de statu Reip.& Relig.in regno Galliæ.

Factum saepe est in obsidionibus urbium fame cogente, ut mures, glires, canes, equos, asinos, coria ovium & boum, paleas, quisquilias diligenter perquisierint et avidissime devorarint, & ab humana tandem carne non abstinuerint, quin quod dictu horrendum est ma-

page.notes: The page has no margin notes. The last word is split at the line end: "ma-" is the printed hyphen, and "tres" is the catchword printed at the right below the last line. Spelling was normalised for u/v and i/j as the rules require (ut, viis, urbium, alii, devorarint). Macrons and tildes were kept as printed. The "ē" in "eundē" and "finē" and the "ō" in "nō" in the printed text were read as tilde marks; they may be misread. The word "herbā" has a macron over the final a and may be a tilde.
